plan.disposition: External/mini-plan LLM review is skip at small complexity per the Phase Matrix (Iterate Spec/Mini-Plan/External LLM Review row) — this run is small

findings.finding: DecisionEntryRow renders the proposal body in a bare <pre> instead of through DocumentMarkdown, the pipeline every other OrgSharedDocs tile uses -- including decision_log.md, which renders the SAME body text (byte-preserved by toLoggedBlock) one click later, through DocumentMarkdown's sanitized rehype-raw pipeline. The 'untrusted body' rationale doesn't hold since the trust level doesn't change pre/post countersign. The client's own EVIDENCE_LINE_RE expects markdown bold syntax (- **Evidence:**), confirming the body is authored as markdown and renders wrong (literal asterisks/hashes) in a <pre>.
findings.suggestion: Render entry.block (minus its header line) through DocumentMarkdown for consistency with decision_log.md's rendering of the same content, or document explicitly why this one tile is exempt.

findings.finding: The row's own summary line already shows {timestamp} - {leadId}, then the raw block underneath repeats the identical header (## [<ts>] <leadId>) as unrendered text.
findings.suggestion: Strip the first line of block before display (or add a header-stripped 'body' field to ProposedDecisionEntry) so the identity is shown once.

findings.finding: entryKey = `${timestamp}|${leadId}` is used as both the React list key and the statuses map key, but the server explicitly allows two distinct proposals to share (timestamp, leadId) (duplicate_identity). Two such entries in the list would collide on React key (console warning, possible DOM node reuse) and share one status slot.
findings.suggestion: Include the array index in the key, e.g. `${timestamp}|${leadId}|${i}`, so duplicate-identity entries still render as distinct rows.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the duplicate_identity fix means a (timestamp, leadId) collision can no longer cause a proposal to be silently discarded — performCountersign's idempotent-retry branch only guarded the count>1 case; a single still-proposed match sharing an already-logged identity was assumed to be safe residual cleanup without comparing bodies, so a genuinely distinct later proposal reusing the identity would be silently deleted and reported as already-countersigned under the old ADR number.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: compare bodyAfterHeader(stillProposed.block) against bodyAfterHeader(existing.block); a mismatch now returns duplicate_identity instead of deleting. Added a regression test in countersign.test.ts covering exactly this scenario.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the Stage-2 fix (index-based entryKey) closes the duplicate-identity collision on the client — every data-testid inside DecisionEntryRow still interpolated only timestamp-leadId with no index, so two duplicate-identity rows still collided on every testid even though the React key/status map key was fixed.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: DecisionEntryRow now takes a rowKey prop (the same index-inclusive entryKey) and every data-testid uses it. Added a test rendering two duplicate-identity entries asserting independently addressable rows/buttons/result banners.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: per-row transient UI state (pending/error/duplicate banners) is stable across a refetch triggered by an unrelated row's action — statuses is keyed by array index; a refetch after a sibling row's success/not-found shifts indices, orphaning another row's non-idle status back to idle.
findings.suggestion: REBUTTAL (not fixed): documented inline next to entryKey. Cosmetic staleness only (a banner resets, no data loss or wrong action), underlying file state is always correct, and reproducing it requires one row mid-error while a sibling independently succeeds in the same instant. Deferred rather than adding a second keying scheme.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: ISO_TIMESTAMP_RE rejects any non-canonical timestamp before it reaches performCountersign — the regex's trailing $ (no /m flag) still matches just before a single trailing newline, so '<valid-ts>\n' passed validation and only failed later, less precisely, as proposal_not_found.
findings.suggestion: FIXED: reject timestamp.includes("\n") explicitly before the regex test, so it 400s as timestamp_invalid.

external_code.disposition: External LLM code review is skip at small complexity per the Phase Matrix — the internal spec/code/doubt subagent cascade runs instead (touches_public_api risk flag)

plan_internal.disposition: internal plan review is medium+ only, this run is small
